Definition: properly, the genitive case of G3588; sometimes used for G5127; of this person:--his.
BiblicalUsage: The form tou has no verse of its own in the Greek text. It is the genitive of the article, and every one of its nearly two thousand occurrences in the New Testament is the article at work — "of the," "of him," "of this" — not a separate demonstrative word. Strong lists it apart, but the Greek text never gives it a token of its own.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe plain speech is the only honest option: to wire this form to a meaning of its own would credit it with every "of the" in the New Testament, and that would not be true.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
